review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Weather conditions, precipitation processes, weather quantities and observations; broaden natural phenomenon beyond physical process and separate forecasts from forecasting.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. NWS and Met Office references independently check meteorological scope. Definitions are not copied verbatim; labels, restrictions and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: New concepts and assertions use U1 with unspecified strength. Keep weather conditions, falling precipitation, deposited materials, measured quantities and informational products distinct. Home contexts and relation grammar remain unchanged.

sense_decisions.scope: A natural phenomenon of the atmosphere; this family can include conditions and processes without identifying them.

sense_decisions.alignment: process rather than amount or material
sense_decisions.scope: Water falling from clouds as droplets or ice particles. Select the physical occurrence, not deposited material, accumulated amount, haste or chemical precipitation.
A short rain episode. Do not equate every shower with heavy downpour or with a shower fixture.
A short snowfall episode; no required wind or heavy-snow threshold.
The falling of hail, distinct from the existing hail-material record 1226. No thunderstorm or temperature threshold is universal.

Rain whose supercooled drops freeze on contact with exposed surfaces. Distinguish it from already frozen ice pellets and from the resulting ice coating. The Russian term is also used in the cited Roshydromet research.
Drizzle that freezes on contact. No rain/drizzle drop-size threshold is encoded.
A precipitation episode with both rain and snow components. Bare sleet is excluded because American usage commonly denotes ice pellets.
Weather characterized by rain. The whole atmospheric condition is distinct from the falling-water process.
Weather characterized by wind. No warning threshold or metaphorical verbose meaning is imported.
Weather with both rain and wind; an explicit shared subtype of the two conditions.
Weather during snowfall, not merely a landscape with old snow on the ground.
Temperature of air at the relevant place and time, distinct from dew-point temperature, apparent temperature and a thermometer.
The fraction of sky covered by clouds. Select a quantitative property, not a cloud object, bad-weather judgment or atmospheric state.
Equivalent liquid-water depth accumulated over a specified area and interval. This is a length quantity, not the falling process or water volume.
Accumulated depth due to liquid rain for a specified place and interval.
Depth of a snow layer. This is distinct from its liquid-water equivalent and from new snowfall amount.

sense_decisions.alignment: distance quantity rather than general perceptibility
sense_decisions.scope: Horizontal distance over which a suitable object can be identified under the relevant observing conditions. Do not reuse the existing truth/semblance record 2797.
Measure air temperature, preserving general temperature-measurement ancestry.
Measure accumulated water-equivalent depth over a specified interval.
Measure the rainfall contribution to accumulated depth.
Measure snow-layer depth rather than assume a constant conversion to water equivalent.
Determine meteorological visibility distance under the applicable observation conditions.
Instrument for precipitation measurement. Its design and preparation determine which precipitation phases can be measured.
Restrict the instrument to measuring rain; do not require a heater or snow-melting capability.
A snow-layer depth instrument, without restricting every design to a ruler, laser or ultrasonic sensor.
A thermometer intended for air-temperature measurement, not an implied dew-point or infrared surface-temperature instrument.
An informational prediction of future development. It is neither the forecasting activity nor a guarantee that the predicted event will occur.
A prediction about future atmospheric conditions; not a report of measurements already made.
The activity of predicting weather. Adapt the dictionary statement-oriented hierarchy to the existing forecasting action.
Observing weather and recording relevant conditions or measurements. Do not require every observation to measure every weather quantity.
Recorded information from an observation, distinct from the observation activity and from a forecast.
Keep the long-term weather-pattern meaning and its natural-phenomenon genus; do not collapse it into current weather or a single averaging interval.
The dictionary material gloss incorrectly speaks of droplets of water vapor. Water droplets are liquid; do not copy that phrase or combine material and phenomenon genera.
Russian metel may involve blowing existing snow without fresh snowfall. Defer its blizzard translation and thresholds; do not force all cases beneath snowfall.
The visibility label and truth/semblance genus are ambiguous. Keep it unchanged pending a dedicated sense split; the meteorological distance is unambiguously separate.
Direction currently mixes spatial orientation and directing verbs. Defer wind direction and vane purposes until that family is reviewed.
The atmosphere/layer part-whole distinction requires a separate review; a stratosphere is not a kind of atmosphere.
Dew is condensed liquid on a surface, not falling precipitation.
The existing frost record is deposited solid material, not every use of frost for freezing weather or the deposition process.

review.limits: No forecast guarantee, regional alert threshold, climate averaging mandate, instrument accuracy, quantitative weather cutoff or universal causal probability. Do not import the bare ambiguous sleet term or the water-vapor-droplet error in the dictionary fog gloss. Fog/cloud material senses, atmospheric layers, wind-direction/space senses, general visibility, freezing deposits, inherited weather percentages and physical genera of other natural phenomena remain queued. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Reject weather/natural-phenomenon exclusion while preserving that ancestry. Broaden natural phenomenon so weather states are not forced to be processes. Preserve all other exclusion rows.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Existing humidity, dew point, pressure, wind speed, measuring tools and forecasting are reused.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
